summary: Intro + console walkthrough focusing on per-route usage lenses, cost-attribution, and Optimize recommendations. Customer wants a pilot to validate cost/latency tradeoffs for chat routes and async batch embeddings. Action: pricing + benchmark script + SSO details.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Collins: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes, is that still good?
[00:06] Maya Chen: Yep that's perfect, thanks. We have Raj and Elena on as well.
[00:10] Avery Collins: Great. Diego from our SE team will do the console demo and then we'll circle back to the pilot and pricing. Diego over to you.
[00:18] Diego Ramos: Cool, thanks Avery. I'm sharing my screen — let me know if that doesn't come through. We're starting in the Redwood Console, this is the usage lens, and first up is a per-route heatmap.
[00:28] Raj Patel: Quick Q — we run three main routes: chat-short, chat-long, and embed-batch. I want to see credit consumed per route and also latency percentiles.
[00:36] Diego Ramos: Totally, that's what this view is for. So up top you can select timeframe, and the route table below shows tokens, p95 latency, failed requests, and cost per thousand. You can click into chat-long here and see the token distribution by model variant.
[00:50] [01:12] Maya Chen: Sorry can you expand the model breakdown? I want to know where the expensive tokens are going.
[01:15] Diego Ramos: Yep — clicking the route shows model churn: hosted gpt-3 style variant for short and a quantized Llama variant for long. You can toggle currency or unit cost — this is a per-token unit cost derived from the active model and hardware, so when you saw a spike last Tuesday that was a fallback to the higher-cost Hosted tier.
[01:35] Elena Voss: That spike — can you tie it to an incident or a fallback? We need to explain that to finance.
[01:38] Diego Ramos: Yeah, there is an events timeline on the right. You can see a capacity fallback at 03:22 where policy routed to Hosted-HighPerf; it annotated the route with the reason.
[01:50] [02:10] Raj Patel: How reliable is that route attribution? We have a messy pipeline — sometimes frontends rewrite routes.
[02:16] Diego Ramos: Good point. Our route attribution uses token-level tagging at the invocation layer — but if you rewrite paths upstream, you can set a route header to preserve mapping. We also provide a mapping CSV upload to reconcile historical logs.
[02:34] Maya Chen: For the pilot we want to understand per-route unit economics and also the effect of batching on embed-batch. Can you show Optimize suggestions?
[02:40] Diego Ramos: Sure, moving over to the Optimize tab — this is where Redwood proposes batching and KV cache settings, and quantization profiles per model. For embed-batch it recommends a 512 request batch and switching to int8 quant for inference to save ~45% on GPU time in our tests.
[02:58] [03:25] Avery Collins: Important to call out that savings depend on latency SLOs — if you need sub-50ms for chat-short then large batch sizes won't work.
[03:34] Maya Chen: We're okay with slightly higher latency on embeddings, but chat-short needs low p50.
[03:39] Diego Ramos: Right — Optimize surfaces recommendations with an expected delta for cost and latency, and an estimated quality impact score based on evals. You can accept suggestions as a policy and they become route-level configs.
[03:52] [04:18] Raj Patel: Security question — how are keys managed? We run everything in GCP and need KMS integration and audit logs.
[04:24] Diego Ramos: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; for Dedicated we can bring your KMS via our connector. Audit logs are available in the Console and can be streamed to your SIEM (Cloud Logging, Splunk). We also have SOC2 type II and ISO cert PDFs we can share.
[04:40] Maya Chen: We'll need SSO — SAML metadata and RBAC for routes so product teams can't blow the budget.
[04:46] Avery Collins: We enforce org-level RBAC and token scoping; you can restrict which routes a token can call and set soft spend guards per token.
[04:55] [05:22] Elena Voss: From finance perspective we need per-route invoicing so we can internal chargeback. Is that possible?
[05:27] Diego Ramos: Yes — we have a per-route cost export and a billing API that maps to internal charge codes. You can pull daily CSVs with route, token counts, model, and cost.
[05:40] [06:05] Maya Chen: Show us a real example — the embed-batch cost trend vs token count.
[06:10] Diego Ramos: Pulling the embed-batch view. See here: you can overlay unit cost and batch size; last month the batch size was 16 and cost per 1k tokens was $X, when they increased batch to 128 in a shadow test cost dropped but p95 increased from 220ms to 540ms.
[06:33] Raj Patel: Hmm 540ms p95 is too high for some UX flows. Could we do batching in background for async?
[06:38] Diego Ramos: Exactly — that's the typical pattern: sync chat short, async batch for embeddings. Our routing policy supports multi-class routing with fallbacks: primary route for low-latency, secondary for low-cost.
[06:52] [07:20] Maya Chen: What about KV cache? For long chat we have repeated prefixes across sessions.
[07:25] Diego Ramos: KV cache is shown per-model; enabling prefix caching reduced tokenization and forward passes in our tests, effective cost reduction depends on repetition rate. You can set TTL and cache size per route. It's also included in Optimize suggestions where we estimate reuse rates by sampling traces.
[07:45] [08:12] Raj Patel: Latency vs cost tradeoff — can Redwood autoscale Dedicated pools to avoid fallbacks?
[08:18] Avery Collins: Dedicated allows reserved pools and burst capacity. You can set autoscale thresholds; if you want strict latency SLOs you can provision reserve capacity and set higher priority. We also support a policy that if reserve is exhausted, requests are rate-limited rather than routed to Hosted.
[08:34] Elena Voss: For procurement we need a baseline cost estimate for 6 months. Can you produce a projection?
[08:40] Avery Collins: Yes, we can produce a projection from current traffic: cost by route, recommended Dedicated commit sizes, and expected savings with Optimize. We'll include 3 scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive.
[08:53] [10:01] Diego Ramos: Showing the scenario export — you can pick expected QPS and model mix and the Console outputs projected monthly spend and percent saved by applying Optimize suggestions.
[10:12] Maya Chen: In your projections, do you factor in quantization risk — i.e., potential quality regression?
[10:18] Diego Ramos: We do. The Optimize module includes a quality delta estimate computed from your eval corpus if you upload one. For customers who want stronger guarantees we run A/B tests and provide automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[10:35] [11:05] Raj Patel: For the pilot, we'd like to run a shadow load for two weeks and compare results across Dedicated small pool vs Hosted. What's the setup?
[11:12] Diego Ramos: We usually spin up a Dedicated trial pool and run identical traffic via split-routing: 10% to Dedicated, 90% to Hosted, measure costs, latencies, and output quality. Our perf script (we'll share) will replay traffic with the same request distribution.
[11:28] Maya Chen: Will that require infrastructure changes? We want minimal dev time.
[11:33] Diego Ramos: Minimal — we'll give you a small SDK snippet to set route headers and toggles. If you use our API directly, it's a header flag to pin route. For more advanced proxying we can provide a sidecar example.
[11:50] [12:40] Elena Voss: About SLAs — what's Redwood Dedicated SLA?
[12:46] Avery Collins: Dedicated SLA is 99.9 up time for the reserved pool and latency SLOs per model class. SLA and credits are part of the Dedicated contract.
[12:54] [13:30] Maya Chen: Any enterprise security reviews we should expect?
[13:35] Avery Collins: We do an initial security questionnaire, then optional on-site/remote architecture review. We'll share SOC2 and the security pack after this call.
[13:47] [14:05] Raj Patel: Can your console emit trace spans for our APM?
[14:10] Diego Ramos: Yes — we have tracing hooks and can export to OpenTelemetry collectors. You can map request ids to your spans.
[14:20] [16:00] Diego Ramos: Back to the Console — here's a deep dive on per-route alerts. You can set cost thresholds to notify Slack and also automated throttles that prevent runaway spend.
[16:12] Maya Chen: Cool — we need a spend guard so Product can iterate without surprising finance.
[16:18] Diego Ramos: You can set soft and hard guards per token or per route. Soft guard will email owners, hard guard will block requests.
[16:28] [18:00] Raj Patel: We saw references to fallback policies earlier — are they rule based?
[18:06] Diego Ramos: Yes, the routing rules are policy DSL-like: selectors by region, latency, customer tier, and explicit model variants. You can compose fallbacks: e.g., first try Dedicated-quant8, then Dedicated-int8, then Hosted-eco.
[18:22] Maya Chen: Let's talk costs: show a month-over-month cost waterfall with applied Optimize changes.
[18:30] Diego Ramos: Switching to the waterfall view — here's baseline, Optimize applied, and your net. In this synthetic example, Optimize saves 28% mostly from batching and quantization on embed-batch and KV cache on chat-long.
[18:55] [21:00] Elena Voss: We need to validate those numbers — what's the confidence interval?
[21:05] Diego Ramos: We provide error bounds derived from sampling variance and hardware variability. For small pilots it's wider; for long runs we'll tighten it.
[21:22] [24:10] Avery Collins: Quick objection we often get: "What if a model upgrade increases token count unexpectedly?" We advise pinning model versions and using rollout policies. You can canary a new model on 2% traffic and monitor token delta alerting.
[24:35] Maya Chen: Great, can you show rollout controls?
[24:40] Diego Ramos: Here's the rollout UI: you can configure canary percentage, progressive ramp, and automatic rollback based on quality deltas or cost thresholds.
[25:05] [27:00] Raj Patel: On the data retention front — can we keep logs on our side?
[27:06] Diego Ramos: Yes, you can export raw request logs to your storage or we can ship to S3/GCS. For Private deployments you control retention entirely.
[27:20] [30:00] Maya Chen: Demo side note — some of the model names look garbled in the transcript, we use internal names so we may rename routes.
[30:06] Diego Ramos: Totally fine — you can alias model names and routes in the Console to match your internal taxonomy.
[30:20] [33:00] Avery Collins: Okay let's summarize and agree next steps. Avery to send pricing and the pilot template, Diego to send benchmark script. Maya to confirm dataset and SSO details. Elena will surface procurement timeline.
[33:07] Maya Chen: Sounds good. One more question — for the pilot do you require data to leave our VPC?
[33:12] Diego Ramos: For Dedicated trials we can do VPC peering or Private deployment; if you require no egress we have an on-prem option as well, but that introduces lead time. For short pilots VPC peering is the common choice.
[33:30] [35:05] Raj Patel: Any gotchas with our infra? We're on GKE with Istio.
[35:10] Diego Ramos: We have a sidecar proxy example that works with Istio; main thing is route header passthrough. We'll share that in the repo link.
[35:22] Avery Collins: I'll put the security pack and SOC2 in the follow-up email.
[35:26] [40:00] Elena Voss: Timeline: if we like the pilot results, we'd probably go for a Dedicated small commit for Q4. Procurement needs the price and the 6-month projection.
[40:12] Avery Collins: Understood. We'll include the 3-scenario projections and Finance can pick.
[40:25] [45:00] Maya Chen: Thanks for the walk-through — the per-route cost lens answered several of our questions.
[45:05] Diego Ramos: Great — I'll drop the benchmark artifacts and the perf script after this call.
[45:12] [50:00] Avery Collins: Final recap in chat: 1) Pricing + pilot terms (Avery), 2) Perf script (Diego), 3) SSO metadata + dataset (Maya), 4) Procurement timeline (Elena).
[50:30] Raj Patel: We'll aim to give answers by next Thursday.
[50:35] Maya Chen: Thanks all.
[50:40] Avery Collins: Thanks everyone — talk soon.
[50:45] [END]
notes: Customer is focused on per-route unit economics and wants a short pilot (shadow split routing)
Key ask: per-route billing exports + spend guards + SSO + KMS
Risk: some routes need very low latency which constrains batching/quant gains
